name: can_grip_top
notes: The 'put this can upside down' beat, top-rim version. Reaches out, hovers, descends to just above the rim, closes the jaws partway as if taking the rim, then ROLLS THE WRIST 75 deg — the motion that reads as inverting the can — opens, unrolls, lifts away and withdraws. The tip stops 2.6 cm above the rim, so this is a pantomime of the grip and the inversion, not a grasp: nothing is lifted and nothing is turned over. Peak 25 deg/s. JOINT1 IS ZERO IN EVERY WAYPOINT (base locked, clamps). Offsets from the resting pose. GEOMETRY, computed with the official i2rt URDF via yam.kinematics and checked against the MuJoCo collision model: the hover pose puts the jaw tip 20.6 cm above the table at 14.8 cm radial reach; the descent puts it 14.8 cm up (top) or 12.4 cm up (lower). A 355ml can is 12.2 cm tall and 6.6 cm across, so EVERY pose here stays above the can's top rim — no pose can strike the can body. The jaws rest at ~65% open, which is NARROWER than a 6.6 cm can, so the gesture opens them to ~85% BEFORE descending and only closes to ~72% (a 6.8 cm gap, ~2 mm clear of the can). Contact is therefore not required and not expected; if the can is a little proud, the jaws touch it at Boris's calibrated cap and nothing more. JAW NUMBERS CORRECTED after measuring the real calibrated stroke: usable travel is 76 mm (not the 96 mm nominal), so a 66 mm can occupies 86.6% of the stroke, not 69%. An earlier draft closed to 72% — that is a 55 mm gap and WOULD have squeezed the can at the force cap. The jaws now open to 98% (74.5 mm) and close only to 91% (69.2 mm), about 3 mm clear of the can. Separately the gripper's torque ceiling is lowered from Boris's calibrated 0.6 Nm (~41 N) to 0.25 Nm (~17 N) for the demo, so even an unintended contact cannot dent an empty can. JAW TARGETS ARE ABSOLUTE (gripper_frame: absolute), unlike the joint columns: a can is 66 mm across regardless of where the jaws are resting, and their resting percent drifts between runs because the open stop is compliant — a relative target resolved past 100% and refused the motion mid-session. Absolute values: 88% neutral, 98% open (74.5 mm), 90% at the 'grip' (68.4 mm, ~2 mm clear of the can). HONEST LIMIT: usable jaw travel is 76 mm and the can is 66 mm, so there is only ~10 mm of margin in the whole stroke — a big visible open-and-close around this can is not physically available. The wrist roll carries the inversion; the jaws only gesture at it.
